checklist: slicc_fs native (the kernel answers the imports)
umask() returns the kernel's 022; umask 027 → open(O_CREAT, 0666) gives 640
open(O_CREAT|O_TRUNC, 0600) → 600; O_EXCL 0640 → 640; openat 0600 → 600; reopen with O_CREAT keeps 755
mkdir 0700 → 700; mkdirat 0777 → 755
fchmod 0644, chmod 0755, fchmodat 0700
fchmodat NOFOLLOW on a symlink → ENOTSUP; chmod of a missing path → ENOENT
read back inside WASIX: stat/fstat report the same bits as coreutils' stat (fd_mode / path_mode); lstat sees the symlink
on a kernel without slicc_fs (1.34.1 and older) the same program exits 0 with upstream behaviour (run-modes.mjs --allow-absent)

-34 (homescoop#770, #629, #559; slicc-kernel#892/#893/#931): test/r33.c in all five variants on slicc-kernel 1.117.3 (R33_KERNEL=1). sigwaitinfo gives a forked child's kill as SI_USER with its pid and our uid, its exit as CLD_EXITED status 7, and pthread_kill as SI_TKILL. An SA_SIGINFO handler runs with the sender and a non-NULL context. flock (slicc.flock): the other end of a pipe conflicts; LOCK_EX on a read-only open excludes a second open (#758); dup and a forked child's inherited descriptor share the lock; EBADF, EINVAL; a handled SIGALRM ends a blocking wait with EINTR, and under SA_RESTART the wait goes on until the holder leaves. poll and ppoll give POLLOUT|POLLERR for a pipe write end without readers (#629), and POLLHUP within 1 s for an events-0 readable read end whose forked writer exits 200 ms in (#559). On the cert kernel (no imports, default and ehpic): -32's sigwait*, SA_SIGINFO with SI_USER and pid 0, and flock's whole-file fcntl fallback, line by line. Every -33 probe row still passes

-34 (homescoop#878, slicc-kernel#957): test/r34.c in all five variants on slicc-kernel 1.120.0 (R34_KERNEL=1). mkfifo through slicc_fs.path_mkfifo makes a FIFO (0666 under umask 022 → 0644). EEXIST for an existing FIFO and for a dangling symlink (not followed); ENOENT for a missing directory. mkfifoat works with a dirfd and with AT_FDCWD plus an absolute path. mknod S_IFIFO is a FIFO, S_IFREG an empty regular file, S_IFCHR EPERM. A forked writer and the reader meet through the FIFO ("hello"). On the cert kernel (no import): mkfifo and mknod(S_IFIFO) are ENOSYS. <sys/stat.h> now declares mkfifo, mkfifoat, mknod and mknodat

-35 (slicc-kernel#975): test/r35.c in all five variants on the cert kernel. A SIGUSR1 handler with SIGUSR2 in sa_mask raises SIGUSR2 and SIGUSR1: neither runs inside it (max depth 1), both run when it returns (order <><>2), and SIGUSR1/SIGUSR2 aren't left blocked. With SA_NODEFER the nested SIGUSR1 runs at once (depth 2) and SIGUSR2 still waits. -34 gives order <2<>> and usr2_inside=1 for both (NEGATIVE.md)

-36 (homescoop#949, #1050, #975, #1057, #950): test/r36.c in all five variants on the cert kernel, plus default/ehpic on slicc-kernel 1.124.8. ppoll, pselect and epoll_pwait with a ready pipe return 1 and leave a SIGUSR1 that their empty mask unblocks pending; it runs at the next unblock. gethostname() equals HOSTNAME, the kernel's node name. poll(POLLIN|POLLOUT) on a reader-less pipe write end gives POLLOUT|POLLERR, and POLLOUT on a socketpair end whose peer closed gives POLLOUT|POLLHUP. r35 accepts either delivery order after the handler returns (<><>2 or <>2<>), and passes on 1.124.8. -35 gives -1 EINTR for the three waits and wasmer.sh for gethostname (NEGATIVE.md)

-36 (homescoop#1059): test/r37.c in all five variants on the cert kernel. siglongjmp lands at its sigsetjmp: a plain jump (3), a jump that restores a saved mask (SIGUSR2 not left blocked), and a jump out of a SIGUSR1 handler with SIGUSR2 in sa_mask. savemask 1 leaves SIGUSR1/SIGUSR2 unblocked; savemask 0 keeps the handler's mask. The asyncify tree has no sigsetjmp and prints so. -35 ends the plain jump with exit 70, [object WebAssembly.Exception]. r28w's 'window masked' row still passes: a handler that runs as the ready check begins makes the call EINTR

-37 (homescoop#1015, #1112): test/r38.c in all five variants on the cert kernel. The S_IF* constants are Linux's: S_IFMT 0170000, SOCK 0140000, LNK 0120000, REG 0100000, BLK 0060000, DIR 0040000, CHR 0020000, FIFO 0010000. stat/lstat/fstat give a regular file 100644, a directory 040755, a symlink 120xxx, a pipe 010xxx and a socketpair end 140xxx; /dev/null and /dev/zero are 020666 by path and by descriptor, and coreutils' stat -c %f agrees (21b6). test/fifo.mjs expects the new bits. -36 prints S_IFMT=160000 S_IFSOCK=160000 S_IFIFO=140000 (NEGATIVE.md)
